title: Closed points in closed subsets of quasi-compact Kolmogorov spaces
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space which is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] (every open covering has a finite subcovering) and Kolmogorov (for any two distinct points $x\neq y$ of $X$ there is an open subset of $X$ containing exactly one of them). Then every nonempty closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ contains a point $z$ such that $\{z\}$ is closed in $X$. In particular, if $X$ is nonempty it has a closed point.

source.place: Topology Lemma 005E (topology-lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point: a nonempty quasi-compact Kolmogorov space has a closed point), applied to $Z$ with the subspace topology (a closed subset of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact, a subspace of a Kolmogorov space is Kolmogorov, and a point closed in the closed subset $Z$ is closed in $X$)
